title: SAP BTP: SAP Task Center
excerpt: Central inbox for approvals across SAP + non-SAP.
body:
## Task Center
BTP service que agrega tasks from multiple sources:
- SAP S/4HANA (Fiori approvals)
- SAP SuccessFactors
- SAP Ariba
- SAP Concur
- Custom apps

User has ONE inbox for all pending approvals.

## Subscribe
BTP cockpit → **Subscriptions → Task Center**.

## Configuración
Each source system connects via connector:
- Configure endpoint URL
- Auth credentials
- Task type mapping

## User experience
- Fiori launchpad tile
- Or standalone Task Center app
- Ver tasks pending por prioridad
- Actúa (approve/reject) directamente

## Deep link
Click task → open source app (S/4, Ariba) con contexto correcto.

## Mobile
Task Center accesible desde SAP Mobile Start app.

## Common flows
- Purchase requisition approval (Ariba/S4)
- Time-off approval (SuccessFactors)
- Expense report approval (Concur)
- Contract approval

## Cost
Subscription per user.

## Alternate
Custom workflow con Build Process Automation.

title: SAP BTP: Mobile Development Kit (MDK)
body:
## MDK
Metadata-driven mobile framework para iOS + Android.

## Ventajas
- Single codebase, cross-platform
- Offline-first (sync when online)
- Enterprise features (MDM, cert-based auth)

## Setup
1. SAP BTP → subscribe Mobile Services
2. VS Code + MDK extension
3. Create MDK project

## Metadata
App defined en JSON files:
- **Pages** — UI layout
- **Actions** — behaviors
- **Rules** — dynamic logic
- **Data models**

Runtime interprets metadata.

## Data source
Connect via BTP destinations (OData, REST).

## Offline
App caches data localmente (SQLite):
- Read offline
- Queue writes
- Sync when online

Conflict resolution config.

## Deploy
### iOS
- Build .ipa
- Distribute via MDM (Intune/Jamf)
- Or App Store (SAP-branded companion app)

### Android
- Build .apk
- Enterprise distribution

## MDM integration
- iOS: Managed configuration
- Android: Android Enterprise

## Notifications
Push notifications via APNs (Apple) / FCM (Google).

## Common issues
- Sync failures — network/backend issues
- App crash — check logs (Splunk)
- Auth expired — refresh tokens

## Alternative
- Native development (Swift, Kotlin) para custom experiences
- SAP Build Apps low-code

title: SAP BTP: workzone (portal)
excerpt: Corporate portal / launchpad aggregating BTP apps.
body:
## SAP Build Work Zone
Successor of SAP Launchpad service. Central portal para users:
- Access apps (Fiori, custom)
- Personalized dashboard
- News / content publishing
- Collaboration

## Editions
- **Standard** — launchpad functionality
- **Advanced** — content + collaboration

## Setup
Subscribe en BTP → activate service.

## Create site
1. Admin → **Sites → New Site**
2. Name, theme
3. Add pages
4. Assign apps to pages
5. Assign roles (who sees what)
6. Publish

## Content sources
- HTML5 apps (from HTML5 App Repository)
- Fiori apps en S/4HANA
- BTP custom apps
- External URLs

## Federated content
Aggregate content from multiple systems:
- S/4HANA on-prem
- S/4HANA Cloud
- Custom BTP apps

Users see single unified inbox.

## Themes
Customize:
- Colors
- Logos
- Header images
- Text

Match corporate branding.

## Roles + permissions
Role collections determine tile visibility:
- 'HR staff' → see HR tiles
- 'Finance' → see FI tiles
- 'Admin' → see everything

## Search
Enterprise search across content:
- App names
- Documents
- News

## Mobile
Responsive UI. Also SAP Mobile Start app pulls content.

## Common issues
- Tile not visible — role mapping
- Slow load — CDN caching config
- Auth loop — trust config wrong

title: SAP BTP: SAP Continuous Integration and Delivery
tags: btp, cicd, sap ci cd, pipeline
body:
## SAP Continuous Integration and Delivery
Managed CI/CD service, alternate a GitHub Actions / Jenkins.

## Subscribe
BTP cockpit → **Subscriptions → SAP Continuous Integration and Delivery**.

## Concepts

### Jobs
CI pipeline definition — steps to build + deploy.

### Credentials
Stored securely (API keys, deploy creds).

### Repositories
Git repos linked (GitHub, GitLab, BitBucket).

## Config
### UI-based
1. Add Git repo
2. Configure job type (CAP, Fiori, HTML5, MTA)
3. Set trigger (push, PR, schedule)
4. Save

### As-code (YAML file en repo)
`.pipeline/config.yml`:
```yaml
stages:
  build:
    npmExecuteEndToEndTests: false
    npmExecuteScripts:
      scripts: ['ci-build']
  deploy:
    cfDeploy:
      apiEndpoint: 'https://api.cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com'
      org: 'my-org'
      space: 'prod'
      credentialsId: 'cf-creds'
```

## Predefined stages
- **build** — install, compile
- **test** — unit tests, coverage
- **security scan** — dependency vuln check
- **quality gate** — SonarQube
- **deploy** — a CF space

## Notifications
On build success/fail:
- Slack
- MS Teams
- Email

## Compare vs GitHub Actions
- SAP CI/CD: opinionated, SAP-optimized, managed
- GitHub Actions: flexible, universal, self-managed

Use SAP CI/CD si equipo not familiar con CI/CD y quiere quick setup.

## Cost
Subscription-based.

## Alternative
- **Piper library** — SAP's Jenkins pipeline library. Reusable in any Jenkins.
- **Cloud-native tools** — Argo CD, Flux (K8s)

title: SAP BTP: SAP Print service
excerpt: Send print jobs desde BTP apps.
body:
## SAP Print Service
Managed printing:
- On-prem printers (via SCC)
- Cloud printers

## Subscribe
BTP → **Subscriptions → SAP Print Service** (o Cloud Printing).

## Config
1. Configure printer:
   - Type: local (SCC), cloud
   - Address
2. Assign to app

## Send job
```javascript
const printService = require('@sap/cloud-printing');

await printService.print({
    document: pdfBuffer,
    printerName: 'floor2-hp',
    copies: 1,
    doubleSided: false
});
```

## SmartForms / Adobe Forms
Generate forms en S/4HANA → PDF → send to BTP print service → physical print.

## Multi-tenant
Different printers per tenant/location.

## Common issues
- Printer offline
- Auth to printer failed
- PDF format not supported (use PDF/A)

title: SAP BTP: SAP AI Core y AI Launchpad
excerpt: Deploy y manage ML models en BTP.
body:
## SAP AI Core
MLOps platform para:
- Train models
- Deploy inference endpoints
- Version + monitor

## Componentes
- **AI Core** — runtime (K8s-based)
- **AI Launchpad** — UI dashboard
- **Generative AI Hub** — LLM access (Claude, GPT-4, Gemini via BTP)

## Provisioning
Subscribe en BTP cockpit.

## Workflow

### 1. Training
- Upload dataset
- Define training config
- Run training job

### 2. Registered model
Model artifact stored

### 3. Deploy
Deploy as inference endpoint:
- HTTP API
- Auto-scaling

### 4. Consume
App calls endpoint via destination.

## Generative AI Hub
Access LLMs sin managing:
- Claude 3.5 Sonnet
- GPT-4
- Gemini 1.5

### Use via API
```javascript
const response = await fetch('https://ai-core-endpoint/models/claude/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
        prompt: 'Summarize this document...',
        maxTokens: 500
    })
});
```

## Joule
SAP's copilot embedded en Fiori, S/4HANA, SuccessFactors. Powered by BTP AI Core.

## Custom AI use cases
- Document extraction (invoice OCR)
- Predictive maintenance
- Demand forecasting
- Chatbots (customer service)

## Common patterns
- Fine-tune LLM on corporate documents
- Custom model deployed to AI Core
- App consumes via HTTPS

## Cost
Based on:
- Compute time
- Storage (models, data)
- API calls

## Governance
- Access control per model
- Audit log
- Data privacy (data used for training)

## Alternatives
- Azure ML
- Google Vertex
- AWS SageMaker

SAP AI Core integrated con SAP data sources naturally.

title: SAP BTP: Document Management Service
excerpt: Managed document repository para business documents.
body:
## Document Management Service
Cloud repository con CMIS (Content Management Interoperability Services) API:
- Store documents (PDF, images, Office files)
- Version history
- Metadata
- Full-text search (optional)

## Create instance
```bash
cf create-service sdm application my-docs
```

## Access
CMIS API endpoints:
```
https://<sdm-endpoint>/browser/{repository-id}/root
```

## Node.js SDK
```bash
npm install @sap/document-management-service
```

```javascript
const { DocumentClient } = require('@sap/document-management-service');
const client = new DocumentClient(credentials);

// Upload
await client.uploadFile({
    folder: '/invoices/2026',
    file: fileBuffer,
    name: 'invoice-12345.pdf',
    contentType: 'application/pdf'
});

// Download
const content = await client.downloadFile('/invoices/2026/invoice-12345.pdf');

// List
const files = await client.listFiles('/invoices/2026');
```

## Metadata
Attach custom properties:
```javascript
await client.setProperties('/invoices/12345.pdf', {
    customerId: 'C-100',
    amount: 1500,
    status: 'approved'
});
```

Searchable.

## Access control
- Roles per folder
- Public/private documents
- Time-limited share links

## Version history
Every update creates version. Revert if needed.

## Integration con S/4HANA / GDS
Use for attachment storage instead of DB BLOB.

## Common use cases
- Attach docs to sales orders
- Employee documents (contracts, IDs)
- Product images
- Compliance docs

## Cost
Storage + API calls.

title: SAP BTP: SAP Cloud ALM
excerpt: Application Lifecycle Management para SAP landscape.
body:
## SAP Cloud ALM
Central ALM:
- Monitor SAP + BTP systems
- Detect issues automatically
- ITSM integration
- Business process monitoring

## Editions
- **Operations** — monitoring + incident mgmt
- **Implementation** — project + change mgmt (for greenfield / migrations)

## Subscribe
Included en SAP Enterprise Support (may cost extra depending contract).

## Setup
1. Provision Cloud ALM tenant
2. Connect managed systems:
   - S/4HANA (on-prem + cloud)
   - Ariba
   - SuccessFactors
   - BTP apps
3. Deploy monitoring content

## Monitoring capabilities
- **Health monitoring** — system availability
- **Job monitoring** — batch jobs
- **Business process monitoring** — end-to-end (order-to-cash)
- **Integration monitoring** — iFlows en Integration Suite
- **User experience monitoring** — synthetic transactions

## Alerts
Rule-based:
- System down
- Job failed
- Business KPI outside threshold

Notifications a email / ticket system.

## ITSM
Integrate ServiceNow, Jira Service Management. Auto-create tickets for issues.

## Analytics
Cross-landscape dashboards. Cross-system correlation.

## Cost
Included en Enterprise Support contract typically. Check yours.

## Alternatives
- Solman (on-prem legacy, being deprecated)
- Custom monitoring stack (Splunk + Grafana + custom)

SAP Cloud ALM is cloud-native successor con less operational overhead.

title: SAP BTP: multi-region / multi-cloud
tags: btp, multi region, multi cloud, ha
excerpt: Deploy en múltiples regiones/proveedores para HA.
body:
## Multi-region setup

### Same subaccount, different services regions
No directamente supported — subaccounts region-locked.

### Multiple subaccounts, different regions
Deploy en:
- Subaccount-US (region: US)
- Subaccount-EU (region: EU)
- Subaccount-APJ (region: APAC)

Apps deployed en cada. DNS o traffic manager routes users based on location.

## Multi-cloud
BTP available en:
- AWS regions
- Azure regions
- GCP (limited)
- Alibaba Cloud (China)

Same code deployable across. But service availability varies (check per service).

## DR (Disaster Recovery)
### Active-passive
- Primary in Frankfurt (EU10)
- Standby en Netherlands (EU20)

On primary failure:
- Update DNS to point to standby
- Users route to standby

RPO/RTO depending on data replication strategy.

### Active-active
Both regions serve traffic simultaneously.
- Session state distributed
- Data replicated real-time

Más complejo pero zero-downtime.

## Data replication

### HANA Cloud multi-region
Enterprise HANA Cloud tier: cross-region replication.
- Automatic failover
- Data consistent (async replication)

### App state
Stateless apps ideal. State en shared storage (Redis, DB).

## Traffic routing

### Global load balancer
- Azure Traffic Manager
- AWS Route 53
- Cloudflare

Route users a nearest healthy region.

### GeoDNS
DNS returns different IP based on user location.

## Compliance
Data residency:
- GDPR requires EU data en EU
- LGPD (Brazil) needs Brazil data locally
- Etc.

Region selection critical.

## Cost
Multiple regions = multiple deployments = higher cost.

Commonly:
- Active primary + warm standby (partial cost)
- Or single region for smaller orgs

## Testing
- **DR drill** annual — actually switch traffic to standby
- Verify data integrity
- Measure actual RTO

## Common issues
- **Config drift** between regions
- **Data inconsistency** during failover
- **DNS propagation** delay

Automate deployment con IaC (Terraform) to keep parity.

title: SAP BTP: dev-to-prod pipeline best practices
tags: btp, pipeline, dev, qa, prod, best practices
body:
## Landscape típico
- **Dev** — feature development, breaks often
- **QA/Test** — validation before prod
- **Prod** — customer-facing

Cada = separate subaccount.

## Cost consideration
Multiplicar todo x3:
- 3 HANA Cloud instances
- 3 XSUAA instances
- 3 app deployments

Optimize:
- Dev: smaller instances
- QA: mid-tier
- Prod: full-tier

## Data
### Data seeding
- Dev: seed with sample data
- QA: recent prod snapshot (anonymized)
- Prod: real data

### Anonymization
Remove/mask PII before copying prod → QA/Dev.

### Refresh cadence
- QA: refresh from prod monthly
- Dev: refresh quarterly (o on-demand)

## Deploy flow
1. Dev auto-deploy (every commit)
2. Feature branch merge → QA deploy
3. QA validation (UAT)
4. QA sign-off → Prod deploy
5. Prod smoke tests
6. Rollback if issues

## Feature flags
Control visibility of new features:
- Deploy to all envs
- Enable in dev, disable en prod initially
- Gradual rollout in prod (10% → 50% → 100%)

## Config differences
Env-specific config via:
- Env vars
- Config files per environment
- BTP destinations (different URLs per subaccount)

**NO hardcode** URLs / creds.

## Approval gates
Deployment pipeline:
- Dev → QA: automatic on merge
- QA → Prod: manual approval + change ticket

## Testing en QA
- End-to-end tests
- Load tests
- Security scans
- Business validation (UAT with actual users)

## Monitoring
Same monitoring stack all environments. Different thresholds:
- Dev: relaxed (allow issues to catch bugs)
- QA: strict (find bugs before prod)
- Prod: very strict (alert on any anomaly)

## Access control
- Dev: broad access (engineers)
- QA: limited (QA + engineers)
- Prod: minimal (ops + on-call)

## Change management
Prod changes tracked:
- Change ticket
- Approval (peer review + management)
- Deployment window
- Rollback plan documented

## Common anti-patterns

### 'Test in prod'
No separation → risky

### Skipping QA
'Small change, going straight to prod' → bugs escape

### Manual deploy
Human error. Use CI/CD.

### Config drift
Dev config diverges from prod → surprises

Use IaC (Terraform, or MTA) para consistent config.

## Best practices summary
- **Separate subaccounts** per env
- **Automated CI/CD**
- **Feature flags** for progressive rollout
- **Anonymized data** en non-prod
- **Change management** for prod
- **Same monitoring** all envs
- **Least privilege** access
- **Rollback rehearsed** regularly
